originality.rationale: Fused retrieval over literal, equivalent, and dominance queries (SerpBase/OpenAlex/Crossref/OpenAIRE, no partial failure) finds no prior stating or implying that every three-ququart stabilizer AME state is LC-equivalent to a weighted graph state. Nearest priors are strictly weaker or disjoint: qubit/prime-dimension stabilizer-to-graph theorems (Van den Nest, Gross school via Helwig Lemma 6) do not cover Z4 where torsion obstructs the general statement; Helwig arXiv:1306.2879 constructs AME graph examples (prime dimensions, existence) but proves no universality over the stabilizer-AME class and no freeness theorem; Looi-Griffiths PRA 84.052306 explicitly restricts to prime/squarefree D, excluding D=4; Wong-Jiang arXiv:2507.09416 decomposes arbitrary-D tripartite stabilizer states only with unitaries beyond Clifford, so it does not imply LC-graph equivalence. No census, table, or database records the (3,4) stabilizer-AME LC classification. The freeness-via-torsion plus explicit LC criterion is substantively new.

General Z4 stabilizer theory admits non-free (torsion) modules, so prime-field arguments do not mechanically imply the AME-subclass result.

The headline claims the converse universality inside the (3,4) AME class via a new obstruction-vanishing argument (AME forces torsion 8). This is a strict logical strengthening requiring the Lemma 1 delta-proof, not a corollary, recomputation, or repackaging.
